entrepreneur

/ahn-truh-pruh-NUR/ — four beats, ending like 'her' with an N: 'NUR' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Entrepreneur is a person who takes on risk to start and build a business.

The entrepreneur risked her savings to open the town's first bubble-tea shop.

Example

At sixteen, Dev noticed that no one in his town delivered groceries to elderly residents. The young entrepreneur spent his savings on a cargo bike, printed flyers, and within a year was managing three helpers and a small fleet.

That is exactly what makes Dev an entrepreneur: he spotted an opportunity, risked his own money, and built a business from nothing. A mere 'worker' does assigned tasks; an entrepreneur creates the enterprise itself and shoulders the risk.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

innovator: An innovator is a person who introduces new ideas or methods — the newness itself is the point. An entrepreneur may copy an approach that is proven elsewhere; what makes an entrepreneur is taking on the risk to start the venture. You can innovate from a salaried lab job without risking a cent.

self-starter: A self-starter is a person who takes action on their own initiative, without waiting to be told — in any role, including a salaried one. An entrepreneur adds two things a self-starter need not have: their own money at risk, and a business being created from nothing.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

employee: a person who works for someone else's business

follower: a person who goes along with others rather than leading

Where it sits · the scale of business ambition — shopkeeper → entrepreneur → magnate

shopkeeper vs. entrepreneur: Shopkeeper is weaker than entrepreneur — a shopkeeper simply runs a store, while an entrepreneur takes real risks to create something new.

magnate vs. entrepreneur: Magnate is stronger than entrepreneur — a magnate has already built a vast business empire, while an entrepreneur may still be launching a first venture.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — entre-

prefix — entre-: between, among (French (from Latin inter))

root — pren(d)

root — pren(d): to take (French (from Latin prehendere))

suffix — -eur

suffix — -eur: one who does (French)

Put it together

Put it together: French entreprendre means 'to undertake' — literally to take something in hand. An entrepreneur is 'one who undertakes' a venture, taking on both the work and the risk.

Use the root in a new word: enterprise

Use the root in a new word: enterprise: The two friends launched a small recycling enterprise from their garage.
